articles.title: In 1953, a New Jersey woman gave away her name and possessions, then spent 28 years walking America; she covered 25,000 miles for peace by 1964
articles.summary: Discover the incredible journey of Mildred Lisette Norman, known as the Peace Pilgrim, who spent 28 years walking across America and beyond to promote peace and self-realization. From her humble beginnings in New Jersey to being nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize, learn about her impactful message and the legacy she left behind.
articles.body: Mildred Lisette Norman set out on a journey on 1 January 1953 that would continue for 28 years under a self-styled name as the Peace Pilgrim. Norman was born in Egg Harbor City, New Jersey, on 18 July 1908, and she left her home along with her identity behind to spread her message through walking and public engagement.According to the Friends of Peace Pilgrim, Norman, the eldest of three children, grew up on a poultry farm alongside her extended family. In 1926, she graduated as a valedictorian of her high school class and found work as a secretary at Liberty Cut Glass Works in her hometown. After a fire ensued at the business in 1929, she obtained another secretarial position at Renault Winery and married Stanley Ryder in 1933. In 1952, aged 44, she became the first woman to complete the entire Appalachian Trail in a single season, an experience that preceded her decision to begin a sustained pilgrimage for peace.From Mildred Norman to Peace PilgrimNorman’s first cross-country pilgrimage started on New Year's Day 1953 when she departed from the Rose Bowl Parade in Pasadena. She set out on her mission wearing a navy-blue tunic that bore her chosen name while handing out leaflets that encouraged peace. According to the New Jersey Hall of Fame, Norman had relinquished any ties that could keep her tethered to worldly possessions and adopted ways that were apt for her lifestyle.Along her pilgrimage, she found sustenance from people she encountered who provided her food and accommodation. She found an outlet for her vision through presentations at schools and churches where she shared her views on peace between nations, environmental responsibility, and the importance of self-peace. As per the Friends of Peace Pilgrim, it wasn’t until 1964 that the feats of her walking became quantifiable when she had accomplished 25,000 miles on foot in Washington, DC. Afterwards, she stopped keeping a tab on her mileage count but continued to travel for 17 years, and her estimated total across the 28 years came to 43,500 miles.Moreover, her travels brought her beyond the shores of the United States, and in 1955, she began a second pilgrimage from San Francisco and walked at least 100 miles in every state and visited each state capital. She also travelled through Mexico and Canada. In 1957, she walked 1,000 miles in Canada, including at least 100 miles in each province. Later journeys took her to Alaska and Hawaii, which she visited for the first time in 1976 through the generosity of an admirer.The final pilgrimage and the work carried on after her deathAs per the Friends of Peace Pilgrim chronological records, her fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh journeys took place in 1966, 1969, 1973, and 1978, respectively. In June 1979, Norman led an educational and inspirational tour of Alaska, followed by a similar tour of Hawaii that took place in June 1980.However, the biggest recognition for her lifelong work came in the Spring of 1981, when a group of church leaders in Memphis, Tennessee, formally nominated her for the Nobel Peace Prize. Nevertheless, her pilgrimage continued until she passed away on 7 July 1981, near Knox, Indiana, in a car accident while she was in transit to a speaking engagement during her seventh cross-country walk.Her work, on the other hand, survived in spite of her death; it went on to have a lasting impact, and a non-profit, all-volunteer organisation was set up by Friends of Peace Pilgrim to commemorate her story and keep her writings in circulation. Subsequently, the organisation published her work, Peace Pilgrim: Her Life and Work in Her Own Words, a collection of her writings, letters, interviews and other material documenting her experiences and spiritual development.You use AI every day. articles.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
articles.summary: The PM's Likud party has alleged foreign interference and said Arab-led parties "stole" the election after his coalition lost its majority.
articles.body:
The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

Netanyahu's Likud accused Israel's Arab-led parties of "stealing" the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Qatar's foreign ministry denied the "ridiculous and dangerous" allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha.

Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament.

The two Arab party lists - The Joint List and the Ra'am - defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc securing 48.

On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been "bribed" to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate "serious suspicions" of foreign interference.

Both Arab parties strongly rejected the claim, with the Arab-majority Joint List alliance saying it was baseless.

The row is being seen by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to delegitimise the Arab parties, thereby making it politically impossible for Eisenkot to join forces with them - which is currently his bloc's only route to power.

Israeli media reported that the CEC had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar's Foreign Ministry "categorically" denied the claims.

Netanyahu and his Likud Party framed the allegations as a "political earthquake" and an "an attack on democracy", aimed at removing their right-wing government.

But the Shin Bet later clarified that their investigation did not implicate an entire community who had voted legally, while acting CEC Director General Dean Livne said there was "no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity."

Eisenkot, who was briefed on the investigation, said "it is too early to determine what happened, or if anything happened at all," and accused Netanyahu of running "an orchestrated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results".

Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: "The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results."

Netanyahu's attacks on Arab voters and parties have been ongoing for days. He spent much of election day posting on social media that high Arab turnout is an "emergency" and a "matter of life or death" for the Israeli right. He also shared AI-generated images of Arab voters at polling stations, in an attempt to encourage right-wingers to get out and vote.

Arab Israelis, many of whom refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel, make up about one fifth of the country.

For years, many boycotted Israeli elections, saying voting would legitimise a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens. But their turnout on Tuesday was inspired by a desire to oust the most right-wing governing coalition in Israel's history, led by Netanyahu.

The final results offer only three plausible options for a government to be formed: a national unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot, a right-wing coalition involving Netanyahu and defectors from Eisenkot's bloc, or an Eisenkot-led government supported by the Arab parties.

Eisenkot and every member of his bloc bar one has previously refused to enter government with Arab parties, but speculation has swirled in recent days that an agreement could yet be reached.

A snap poll conducted by Hebrew University showed that the most popular option for voters from every party in the opposition bloc was for Eisenkot to form a minority government with Ra'am, and supported from outside by the Joint List.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart: Actor who moved effortlessly between Star Trek and Shakespeare
articles.summary: The English actor began his career on stage before finding fame as the captain of the USS Enterprise.
articles.body:
Sir Patrick Stewart, who has died at the age of 86, was a stage and screen great who balanced Hollywood stardom with an equally stellar career in classical theatre.

While many actors are typecast, he moved effortlessly from Shakespeare and Dickens to the command of the USS Enterprise and his famous wheelchair in X-Men.

In a career that spanned seven decades, Sir Patrick received multiple awards, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II.

One of the world's most versatile actors, he mastered both comedy and tragedy, science-fiction and historical drama - despite the entertainment industry's traditional dislike of bald heads.

Patrick Hewes Stewart was born in Mirfield in the West Riding of Yorkshire on 13 July 1940.

His mother Gladys was a textile worker. She was active in amateur dramatics and encouraged her three sons to take part.

His father was a former Sergeant Major in the Parachute Regiment whose experience during the wartime evacuation of Dunkirk had shredded his mental health.

"My father was a very potent individual," Stewart later recalled. "It was said that when he strode on to the parade ground, birds stopped singing."

But Alfred Stewart had become a quick-tempered man, suffering from what would now be called post traumatic stress.

He was prone to drink and often took out his frustrations on his family - although Patrick himself was never the target of his fists.

Young Patrick's love of drama developed at school when one of his teachers introduced him to Shakespeare and encouraged him to perform.

His first public performance was in a local church production of Cinderella.

He found the predictability of dramatic performances a welcome change form the turmoil of his home life.

He left school at 15 and eventually got a job as a journalist and obituary writer on the Dewsbury Reporter.

He also threw himself enthusiastically into the flourishing local theatre. "I used to recite Shakespeare from memory," he said. "I just learned all these big speeches."

But he found it impossible to concentrate on both his job and his acting. Eventually his editor told him to choose between journalism and the "foolhardy" acting.

Stewart picked up his typewriter and walked out.

At the age of 18, he had the traumatic experience of losing all his hair, a huge blow to an aspiring actor and self-conscious teenager - who worried that girls would no longer find him attractive.

He won a scholarship to the Bristol Old Vic and later joined the Royal Shakespeare Company - playing a variety of roles across the company's repertoire.

And when not appearing as Oberon or Enobarbus, he made his TV debut as a fireman in a 1967 episode of soap opera Coronation Street.

His Broadway debut came in 1970 as Snout in Peter Brook's critically acclaimed production of A Midsummer Night's Dream.

Over the next two decades, Stewart appeared in a variety of television roles without threatening to become a major star.

In 1974, he played Lenin in the BBC's 13-part drama series The Fall of Eagles.

He was a conspiratorial Roman soldier in the hugely popular I, Claudius and a Soviet spy in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy and Smiley's People.

In 1984, Stewart left the RSC and moved to the National Theatre. Now in his mid-40s, he had only ever been unemployed for three weeks, but was rarely cast as a main character.

He'd landed a number of minor film roles: including playing Guinevere's father in Excalibur, a minstrel in Dune, and a riding instructor in Little Lord Fauntleroy.

And he was the voice of a small character in the animated film of Richard Adams' novel The Plague Dogs.

But even he described the first half of his career as "sound but never spectacular".

Then came the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard.

A producer named Robert L Justman was intent on reviving the Star Trek franchise, and was looking for a successor to William Shatner's legendary James T Kirk.

He had hoped to find a sexy, hirsute Frenchman to play the role - but chanced upon Stewart giving a lecture to his wife's Shakespeare class in Los Angeles.

Justman turned to his wife. "I said I think I've found our new captain," he said.

He knew nothing about the original Star Trek and his great friend Sir Ian McKellen, told him not to throw his stage career away on a wild goose chase into space.

But in need of a boost to his finances, Stewart signed a six-year contract, firmly believing the show wouldn't last and he'd be back on the boards before long.

"Everybody told me it would be a flop," he recalled. "A friend of mine said, 'Get a suntan, make some money, go home.'"

He was, however, pleased that the producers didn't mind his baldness.

He'd tried wearing a wig in early screen tests, but it looked ratty and - in the end - Star Trek's founder Gene Roddenberry told him to ditch it.

"In the 24th Century, they wouldn't care if Picard was bald," he said.

Stewart, who was billed by the New York Times as "an unknown British Shakespearean actor", found it hard adapting to his new job.

After his stage experiences, he found the 20 hours a day on set tiring, and he also struggled to work with a fairly laid-back and fun-loving US cast.

His decision to call his fellow actors together and give them a lecture about behaving more seriously failed to gain him popularity.

"It was really awful, being dressed down by the captain," said Brent Spiner, who played Data, the android. "We really thought, 'Well, please, get over it'."

Eventually Stewart softened, insisting that every member of the cast told at least one joke a day.

Despite his initial scepticism, Star Trek: The Next Generation both survived and prospered - making its star a very wealthy man.

Captain Picard was supposed to be French, but displayed a surprisingly English regard for both Shakespeare and Earl Grey tea.

And, after playing all those Shakespearean princes and dukes on the London stage, Stewart became fiercely proud of him, and of the show's ability to connect with younger audiences.

In addition to the television series, Stewart played Picard in four Star Trek films. But while commanding the Enterprise, he managed not neglect the theatre.

With his new-found celebrity, the parts he was offered improved greatly.

For years, he performed a one-man version of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol on Broadway - playing all 40 characters.

In 1995, he appeared as Prospero in a memorable performance of The Tempest and, two years later, he starred as Othello - who he presented as a white mercenary in a black African nation.

But his Star Trek success limited the roles that Hollywood was prepared to offer him.

"No director wanted to cast this grand, deep-voiced, bald English guy," he told the Times. "Because everybody knew he was Picard and couldn't possibly be anybody else."

Eventually, he took the role of Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film franchise, essentially playing a telepathic Picard in a wheelchair.

His co-star was Sir Ian McKellen - the friend who'd warned him to avoid Hollywood - in the metal-bending role of Magneto.

Alongside his work in America, he won critical acclaim opposite Harriet Walter in Antony and Cleopatra in 2007.

And, in the same year, he played Macbeth for the first time - despite a 30-year age gap between him and Kate Fleetwood, playing Lady Macbeth.

Critic Nicholas de Jongh decided it was "the best Macbeth I have ever seen", and hailed him as "one of our finest Shakespearean actors".

In 2010, Stewart was awarded a knighthood for his services to drama.

In 2009, he teamed up with Sir Ian again in Waiting For Godot.

It was a moment of personal fulfilment for Sir Patrick who, as an awed teenager, remembered watching Peter O'Toole in the play at the Bristol Old Vic.

His deep and authoritative voice made him much in demand for voice-over roles - including a reprise of his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek video games.

One female interviewer once gushed that "just hearing him order breakfast is rather thrilling".

He also voiced a host of TV commercials both in Britain and the USA.

Away from acting, he was a passionate political activist and a long-time supporter of the Labour Party, as well as a campaigner for victims of domestic abuse.

In 2013, he married his third wife - singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell - in Nevada.

Sir Ian McKellen officiated at the ceremony, which had to be restaged at a Los Angeles restaurant when someone discovered that his legal power to do so did not extend to the Silver State.

A year later, the two knights took their talents to Broadway, alternating performances of Waiting for Godot with Harold Pinter's No Man's Land.

Sir Patrick made a video for Amnesty International on the subject of domestic violence, referencing his father's brutality towards his mother.

Once named the third greatest Yorkshireman after Michael Palin and Sean Bean, he never lost touch with his roots - keeping a house in God's Own Country, and remaining a lifelong supporter of Huddersfield Town football club.

Forthcoming projects had included a final performance as Professor Charles Xavier in Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday, which will be released this Christmas.

And, if millions remember him only as the somewhat taciturn commander of the USS Enterprise, that prospect was not something that worried him.

"For huge numbers of people I will always be Jean-Luc Picard, and that's fine," he said. "I really believe we created an admirable individual."

articles.title: King Charles in Guyana as Bahamas visit declared 'diplomatic success'
articles.summary: As the King left the Bahamas his spokesman said the islands had "a special place in the King's heart".
articles.body:
King Charles has arrived in Guyana for the second leg of his Caribbean tour, following a visit to the Bahamas which Buckingham Palace described as a "sensitive balancing act" and "diplomatic success".

The main themes of the two-day state visit to Guyana will be the environment and sustainability - alongside the growing commercial ties between the UK and Guyana.

The King is due to have an audience with the country's President, Irfaan Ali, and will attend a state reception celebrating the 60 year bilateral relationship between the two countries.

After visiting Guyana, King Charles will visit Antigua and Bermuda where he will open a major Commonwealth leaders summit in his role as the head of the "family of nations".

Guyana - formerly British Guiana - is the world's fastest growing economy due to the discovery of oil reserves there in 2015.

More than four fifths of Guyana is covered by rainforest and it has one of the lowest rates of deforestation in the world.

Cultural exchanges will also feature with a group of bagpipers from the National Piping Centre in Scotland joining the royal tour.

As the King left the Bahamas on Thursday to fly to Guyana for the second leg of his Caribbean tour, his spokesman said the islands had "a special place in the King's heart."

"The great wall of cheers he received when greeting crowds will echo long in his memory - and be a source of tremendous pride and encouragement as the tour continues to Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda."

The two day trip to the Bahamas saw the King meet young boxers, environmentalists and politicians.

He also joined the dancing in a Junkanoo parade to celebrate island life.

But in his only public speech of the tour so far, delivered during his first engagement in the Bahamas, the King referenced the UK's involvement in the slave trade acknowledging the "suffering of the past."

His spokesman said: "The King had hoped, the visit proved an opportunity to celebrate and reaffirm the modern partnership between The Bahamas and the UK. And to address the shared challenges of the future and also to acknowledge the great injustices of the past in a respectful way."

The tour comes amidst renewed calls from Caribbean nations for Britain to apologise for its role in the slave trade and to offer reparations - compensation from those countries who profited from the trade in enslaved men and women.

A small number of protesters were at some of the King's engagements in the Bahamas, with campaigners holding signs saying "pay us what you owe us" but their presence did not disrupt events.

The Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting (CHOGM) being held in Antigua and Barbuda from 1 November will discuss the legacy of slavery. The King will deliver a speech as Head of the Commonwealth.

articles.title: Palestinians injured, arrested in Israeli raids across West Bank
articles.summary: This comes as more than 3,300 Palestinians are forced from homes in Hebron as Israel’s military offensive continues.
articles.body:
Israeli forces and settlers have escalated pogroms and raids across the occupied West Bank, attacking and injuring Palestinians, restricting their movement, carrying out arrests and demolishing homes.

This comes as a military offensive and siege on the Hebron governorate entered its seventh day – an operation that has displaced or besieged hundreds of Palestinian families and kept tens of thousands of students out of classrooms.

In the Qalandiya refugee camp just north of occupied East Jerusalem, Israeli forces carried out a raid that triggered clashes on Thursday. Two children were wounded, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said.

It said its teams treated a 15-year-old boy who was shot with live ammunition in both legs, and a child, aged 12, who was injured by live-bullet fragments. Both were taken to hospital.

In a separate incident, Israeli soldiers and settlers beat disabled Palestinian Mohammad Ahmad Ayesh Thawabta in the village of al-Maniya, southeast of Bethlehem, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

In the northern West Bank, Israeli forces detained 13 Palestinians, including three brothers, in raids before dawn on Thursday, the Palestinian Prisoners Media Office and local sources said. Most of the raids were in the Nablus governorate, where soldiers searched homes and harassed families.

In Hebron, Israeli forces continued raids and closures that began last week after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a gun attack. Both Palestinian suspects were also killed.

Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said on Thursday that 537 families, comprising 3,361 people, have been forced from their homes, Wafa reported.

They include 232 infants, 326 older people, 147 pregnant or breastfeeding women and 213 people with chronic illnesses. Municipal figures put the total number affected, including those under siege, at about 5,000 people from 780 families.

Dudin said the offensive has disrupted education for about 262,000 students across 589 schools in the governorate this week, forcing schools to move to remote learning. Officials estimated daily economic losses at 10 million to 12 million shekels ($3.2m to $3.9m).

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said Israeli forces detained 110 Palestinians in the governorate from Friday to Wednesday. Soldiers beat two men in Dura and Wad al-Saman and arrested two brothers while they were ploughing their land east of Yatta, it said. Israeli forces also raided homes in Taffuh and Halhul, and settlers attacked vehicles at the city’s closed northern entrance, it added.

In nearby Masafer Yatta, armed settlers attacked US journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two activists in the village of Umm al-Khair on Wednesday. Russian activist Adele Shoko said on X that the settlers beat and threatened them and stole their equipment and Nathaniel was pepper-sprayed and arrested.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said Israeli forces are still operating in Hebron, blocking access and imposing tight restrictions on movement across the governorate.

They are “disrupting Palestinians’ access to livelihoods, education and healthcare. Most displaced families are staying with relatives,” OCHA said, calling for the prevention of further forced displacements and demolitions.

Israeli forces also demolished memorials to Palestinians in several parts of the Hebron governorate on Thursday. In Dura, south of Hebron city, soldiers fired a heavy barrage of tear gas before bulldozing a mural bearing the images of several of the town’s dead, including Bajis Abu Atwan, who was killed in the 1970s.

The targeting of memorials “appears to be a new pattern recently adopted by Israeli forces across all West Bank governorates – though at a higher rate here in Hebron”, Al Jazeera’s Muntasir Nassar said, reporting from Dura.

Israeli military and settler attacks across the West Bank have intensified since Israel’s war on Gaza began in October 2023.

articles.title: Korean scalp facials are the latest K-beauty trend, but what do they actually do? I asked experts
articles.summary: The Korean scalp facial can be used to treat scalp issues like oiliness, dryness, thinning hair and more — I asked experts for the best way to try one at home.
articles.body: Despite the name, facials aren’t limited to just your face; in fact, they can benefit your scalp, too. The Korean scalp facial is the latest in a long line of trending K-beauty routines, and for good reason: Those who’ve tried it rave about how it benefits their overall hair and scalp health. To find out more about what a Korean scalp facial does, I spoke to Madeline June, a board-certified nurse practitioner specializing in cosmetic dermatology and aesthetic medicine at The Well Westlake, and Christina Kim, a board-certified esthetician and founder of dupï studio. I also compiled a list of expert- and NBC Selected editor-recommended cleansers, exfoliants, conditioners and treatments you can use to get one at home. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best Korean scalp facial products Best shampoo Cleansers in a Korean scalp facial should be able to remove buildup without stripping the scalp, says June. This shampoo comes recommended by dermatologists in our guide to K-beauty hair because it’s stimulating and gentle. It has biotin to help reduce breakage and rosemary oil to stimulate blood flow to your scalp, which brings more nutrients to your hair follicles and helps grow out your hair, according to the brand. It’s free of parabens, sulfates and silicones, and it’s safe for color-treated hair. Best scalp scrub A gentle scalp exfoliant is a key step in a Korean scalp facial, and this Aromatica scalp scrub helps to detox your scalp by removing dead skin cells and oily residue. It has rosemary leaf extract, which helps to reduce itchiness and dryness and stimulates blood flow to help your hair grow healthier, according to the brand. It also has natural sea salt, which removes dead skin, making it great for dry, flaky scalps. Best liquid exfoliant If you’re not a fan of physically exfoliating your skin, a liquid exfoliant is a great alternative to a scrub. This one is made to help balance your scalp’s oiliness and remove sebum, dead skin and other buildup, according to the brand. You can apply it directly to your scalp before shampooing, massaging it in gently, and rinse it out as normal. It also has rosemary extract to stimulate your scalp, along with vitamin E and citric acid to help soothe the skin. Best conditioner Conditioners help to strengthen and add moisture back to your hair after shampooing, and this one from Ryo is designed to reduce breakage and thicken hair, according to the brand. It has caffeine extract to reduce hair loss and Korean ginseng to help treat signs of aging on the scalp, according to Ryo. It’s also free of mineral oil, fragrance and sulfates, is also pH-balanced to help protect your scalp’s biome, making it great for sensitive skin. It’s also free from mineral oil, fragrance and sulfates. Best hair serum Ampoules are highly-concentrated serums that are very popular in the K-beauty world. This ampoule in particular is great for dry or irritated scalps because it has an exosome complex that helps keep your hair and scalp moisturized, according to the brand. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin loves how easy the serum is to apply; it has a built-in, gua sha-inspired scalp brush that helps you massage the serum deeper into your scalp and roots. The brush has comb-like bristles that Malin says makes it easy to work through her hair, and she likes that the twist-top keeps too much product from spilling out. For best results, use one to two times daily before styling on either wet or dry hair. Best scalp mask Although most conditioners are best concentrated on the lengths and ends of your hair, Kim suggests using this mask specifically for treating your scalp. It has biotin, hydrolyzed keratin and peptides to help strengthen strands and improve hair elasticity, which is your hair’s ability to stretch and bounce back into shape, according to the brand. It also includes amino acids to help retain moisture, and can be used daily since it’s lightweight, making it especially good for dry or thinning hair. Best hair finishing oil This Mise en Scene option is a great finishing oil to use on your hair before styling it because it doubles as both a moisturizing oil and a heat protectant. It can protect your hair against heat up to 446 degrees Fahrenheit, according to the brand, and it has seven kinds of oils, including olive, coconut and jojoba, to moisturize. It’s also lightweight enough to prevent any greasy residue, layers well with other products and works for all hair types. Best scalp leave-in oil This scalp leave-in serum from Dr. Groot, one of our favorite K-beauty hair care brands, helps keep your scalp hydrated between washes. It has biotin and rosemary oil to strengthen and thicken your hair from the roots, plus it works for all hair types. It’s highly rated with a 4.5-star average rating from nearly 200 reviews at Sephora, and reviewers say the oil is lightweight, non-greasy and doesn’t leave any residue. Best scalp massager Scalp massages are great for supporting your follicle health, and this gua sha tool is made from a smooth, natural jade that helps to massage products deeper into your skin. It also helps stimulate blood flow and release tension around your scalp. The brand recommends dividing your hair into sections after washing and drying, then massaging the product into your scalp using long, gentle strokes of the tool. What is a Korean scalp facial? A Korean scalp facial is basically a skin care-focused treatment for the scalp, according to my experts. “A Korean scalp facial applies the same principles used in Korean facial care, including gentle exfoliation, hydration, barrier support and massaging, but to the scalp,” says Kim. “This is often described as the ‘skinification’ of scalp care because the scalp is skin and deserves more than shampoo alone.”. Depending on the treatment, scalp facials can address issues like product buildup, excess oil, dry or flaky skin, congestion around the follicles and scalp irritation, says June. “It’s less about treating the hair shaft itself and more about caring for the skin underneath the hair,” she says. However, despite its usefulness when addressing scalp and skin support, Kim warns against using Korean scalp facials as a substitute for medical treatment. “It’s not a medical treatment for hair loss, psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis or other scalp disorders,” she says. “Sudden shedding, painful inflammation, sores or persistent scaling should be evaluated by a dermatologist.” How to do the Korean scalp facial at home Below are the steps for a Korean scalp facial you’d get at a spa or hair salon, according to my experts. Although not all steps are necessary for an at-home treatment (for example, the scalp analysis step), you can still do most of these from the comfort of your home using the right products. Scalp analysis: During this step, the scalp is examined to look at oiliness, dryness, buildup, flaking or irritation and determine what type of treatment is appropriate, says June. (More on scalp facials and different scalp types below.)Pre-cleanse or oil treatment: Prior to cleansing, some treatments begin with a lightweight oil or scalp treatment to help loosen buildup and condition the scalp.Scalp cleansing: Use a gentle scalp shampoo (which are shampoos with ingredients targeted toward scalp health, like salicylic acid and rosemary extract) to remove oil, sweat and product buildup without stripping the scalp of its natural moisture.Exfoliation: Following the cleansing, a scalp exfoliant is used to gently remove dead skin cells and buildup around the hair follicles. “This step should be gentle, since aggressive scrubbing can irritate the scalp,” says June. Some common exfoliating ingredients include salicylic acid, tea tree oil and peppermint extract. Scalp treatment or mask: Depending on your specific needs, you can use a hydrating, soothing or balancing treatment. For example, if you’re looking to hydrate a dry scalp, look for barrier-supporting ingredients like glycerin, panthenol, beta-glucan ceramides or urea, says Kim. Scalp massage: Both June and Kim emphasize the importance of massaging your scalp, which helps distribute the products on your scalp. At her studio, Kim’s dry scalp facial focuses heavily on massage, which she says helps release tension around connected areas of the neck, shoulders, temples and scalp fascia, while also adding on lymphatic techniques and hitting acu-pressure points. “This prepares the client to relax and acknowledges that scalp tightness can be connected to tension held elsewhere,” she says.Rinse and conditioning: After the massage, thoroughly rinse the products from your hair and use a conditioner or deep conditioner as needed, says June.Final scalp or hair treatment: Finally, you can finish the treatment with a lightweight serum, tonic or leave-in product, which June says can help hydrate and soothe your scalp. How often should you do a scalp facial at home? How often you do a scalp treatment will depend on your scalp issues and what you use to treat them. However, June says that every four to six weeks is a reasonable amount for a healthy scalp. “At home, gentle cleansing can be part of your regular hair routine, while exfoliation should be much less frequent, often around once every one to two weeks if your scalp tolerates it,” she says. Kim agrees, and says that over-cleaning, over-exfoliation and excessive manipulation can actually result in worsening your scalp issues. “The best routine is one that keeps the scalp consistently comfortable, hydrated and balanced,” she says. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. articles.title: LA residents near famous Hollywood sign fed up with over-saturation of tourists and illegal vendors
articles.summary: Hollywood Hills residents filed a public nuisance complaint against Karen Bass, alleging unchecked tourism turned the area into a public toilet.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Los Angeles residents living near the iconic Hollywood sign have filed a public nuisance complaint over what they describe as out-of-control tourist activity that has turned the area adjacent to the landmark into a "public toilet." Multiple residents of Hollywood Hills neighborhoods filed a complaint Monday in Los Angeles Superior Court against the city of Los Angeles, Mayor Karen Bass and City Councilwoman Nithya Raman, alleging that officials have allowed the area near the sign to become a public nuisance. State law defines a public nuisance as "anything which is injurious to health, … or is indecent or offensive to the senses, or an obstruction to the free use of property, so as to interfere with the comfortable enjoyment of life or property, or unlawfully obstructs the free passage or use, in the customary manner, of … any public park, square, street, or highway." POPULAR BEACH TOWN REJECTS NOISE, TRASH AND TRAFFIC AS IT WEIGHS STRICTER VACATION RENTAL RULES According to the complaint, residents have cited illegal street vending and dumping, along with "public urination and defecation that occur regularly on the City’s property." They also point to increased traffic on surrounding streets and what they describe as an unacceptable risk of devastating fires and gridlock that severely limits their ability to leave their homes. Visitors, they say, routinely smoke cigarettes and throw their cigarette butts into the grass, despite prohibitions against smoking and the significant fire hazard it poses. Likewise, if a fire were to break out — as has happened in the past — increased traffic could prevent fire trucks from reaching their destinations. POPULAR VACATION HOT SPOTS SLAP LIMITS ON TOURIST RENTALS, DRIVING AND MORE TO PROTECT 'STUNNING' SPACES Residents allege that the city is liable because it controls the land where the nuisance conditions exist. They claim the city has actively promoted the area to tourists for years while failing to take reasonable steps to control the impact of increasing numbers of visitors and vendors, as well as the numerous nuisance conditions and safety risks. They also cite increasing obstructions on the narrow neighborhood streets and other blights that they say are "indecent and offensive to the senses." ONCE-HIDDEN COASTAL TOWN FACING DISRUPTION AS SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS TRANSFORM LOCAL LIFE Fox News Digital reached out to Bass and Raman for comment. Raman represents City Council District 4, which includes the Hollywood Hills. The impact of a glut of tourists visiting the Hollywood Hills has long plagued the area, creating safety and quality-of-life concerns for residents. STUNNING VACATION HOT SPOT TURNS INTO OVERCROWDED NIGHTMARE AS TOURISTS FLOOD STREETS "This was a problem 20 years ago—tourists driving into the Hollywood Hills to take pictures of the Hollywood sign or hiking up to it after driving as close to the sign as possible," former Hollywood United Neighborhood Council board member Chuck Suhayda told Fox News Digital. "It caused massive traffic jams and parking problems." Suhayda served on the board for more than a decade. Access to what is known as the Hollywood Hills Neighborhoods — which includes Hollywoodland, Lake Hollywood Estates and Hollywood Knolls — is restricted by the area’s geography. The roads are winding, lack sidewalks and average only about 18 feet in width. The over-saturation of tourists and the corresponding hazards were exacerbated in September 2011, when a "viewing site" of the sign at the intersection of Canyon Lake Drive and Mulholland Highway was cleared of brush on both sides of the street by Council District 4 staff. The goal was to promote tourism by creating a site now known as "Hollywood Sign Lookout." POPULAR DESTINATION CRACKS DOWN HARD ON TOURISTS AS NEW LIMITS THREATEN SUMMER GETAWAYS The area is zoned as open space and separates two residential zones designated for single-family homes. Residents say it has since become inundated with tourists, illegal street vendors and crippling traffic, leading to increased congestion on surrounding streets. FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY In its own documents, the city has admitted that the current situation is "unsustainable." However, residents say officials have ignored the city’s role in promoting Lake Hollywood Park, the viewing site and even the Hollywood Hills Neighborhoods, which they describe as landmarks in their own right—not only because they offer views of the Hollywood sign, but also because of their iconic architecture, steep landscapes and vistas of the Los Angeles basin. articles.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Machado calls for elections upon return
articles.summary: Machado, who was in exile for nearly a year, said the transition in Venezuela's government would be  "irreversible, organised, pacific".
articles.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado is calling for elections to be held next year.

During a news conference in Caracas on Thursday, the Nobel Peace Prize winner said the country's move toward democracy was "irreversible".

She also thanked the Trump administration for opening the "floodgate to freedom" by capturing her opponent, former President Nicolás Maduro.

The same day, Venezuela's interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, said elections would be held and that her government should oversee a "transition of this magnitude" - which Machado dismissed as illogical. Rodríguez, who was Maduro's vice-president, did not set a date for voting.

Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile

Machado said there would be elections in 2027, but also did not offer an exact timeline.

The transition in Venezuela would be "irreversible, organised, pacific", Machado said standing before a slogan which read "Let Us Be Free".

Her return to the country comes after she repeatedly made earlier efforts to re-enter Venezuela, and failed.

Last year Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat and in darkness to travel to Norway and accept the Nobel Peace Prize. Soon after, in January, the US seized Maduro.

The Trump administration then backed Rodríguez as leader. She was sworn in as interim president and later signed an oil deal that granted favourable terms to the US.

Although it remains unclear what Machado plans to do next, she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held. Her ability to return to her country was contingent on approval from the Trump administration.

Speaking about her return, Machado said she had heard one word repeated by the thousands of supporters who thronged her route into the capital - freedom.

"I come to carry out a task and complete a mandate," she said.

The opposition leader said she had not received a message or invitation to meet from Rodríguez, and would not personally participate in election negotiations between opposition representatives and the government.

But she wished them well in their work, she said, in order to see the electoral body reformed so that every Venezuelan, inside the country and abroad, could vote.

Shortly before Machado's news conference, Rodríguez delivered a speech in a conciliatory tone, saying she had "instructed the security agencies that no one be detained without judicial order, except in cases of flagrant commission of crimes".

Rodríguez also spoke of "the doors being open" in Venezuela to returning exiles and talked of dialogue and building consensus.

articles.title: Palestinians face growing bans from Al-Aqsa as Israel tightens control
articles.summary: As Israel renews a ban on Al-Aqsa imam, Islamic Waqf officials warn of shrinking authority at Muslim holy site.
articles.body:
For more than two years, Sheikh Ekrima Sabri has been barred from occupied East Jerusalem’s Al-Aqsa Mosque, unable to pray or deliver sermons at the holy site.

And with his latest exclusion order extending the ban until April 2027, the Palestinian preacher – the head of the Higher Islamic Council in Jerusalem – is among those facing Israeli restrictions at the site – the third holiest in Islam and a Palestinian national symbol.

Sabri has faced repeated exclusion orders since August 2024. The latest order, issued on October 20, prevents Sabri from praying or delivering sermons at Al-Aqsa until April 2027.

At the same time, far-right Jewish religious activists have increasingly been allowed to pray at the site under Israeli police protection, going against a longstanding status quo and opposition from ultra-Orthodox Jewish religious authorities.

The restrictions began after Israeli police detained Sabri in August 2024 over a sermon in which he mourned the Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh, who was assassinated by Israel.

Sabri, one of the most prominent Palestinians in East Jerusalem, has faced repeated Israeli interrogations.

Palestinians say this is part of a campaign against them at Al-Aqsa. The Wadi Hilweh Information Center, a Palestinian human rights monitoring group, says Israeli authorities have issued more than 1,000 exclusion orders barring Palestinians from Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Old City since the beginning of 2026, including against religious figures and Islamic Waqf employees.

The centre reported an increase in exclusion orders ahead of Jewish holidays, documenting more than 40 issued over five days in early September.

Sabri told Al Jazeera that the latest extension was the fifth time Israeli authorities have issued an exclusion order against him.

He described the decision as unjust, illegal, inhumane and uncivilised, saying it was intended to silence those speaking out about Al-Aqsa.

Sabri said that he would continue defending Al-Aqsa despite the restrictions, describing the mosque as an integral part of his Islamic faith.

“These measures are aimed at diminishing the Palestinian presence at the mosque, while simultaneously allowing settlers to carry out incursions in large numbers ,” Sabri said. “Such actions represent an aggressive policy targeting the Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Islamic presence within it.”

Ibrahim al-Natsheh was released by Israeli police earlier this month after spending a week in detention after he was arrested while attending funeral prayers for his cousin at Al-Aqsa Mosque.

He told Al Jazeera that officers took him to a police room and handed him a six-month exclusion order barring him from East Jerusalem’s Old City. He said no specific charge was brought against him.

According to al-Natsheh, the order warns that he could face arrest and further penalties, including a fine or imprisonment, if he enters the prohibited area.

Al-Natsheh said he has received so many exclusion orders that he has lost count. He said the restrictions began about nine years ago, following an Israeli crackdown on Islamic study circles at the mosque.

Palestinian students, teachers and activists associated with the activities have faced arrests and exclusion orders.

“The orders banning us from the mosque provide no specific reason; they simply cite ‘disturbing the peace’, even though we are there solely to pray,” al-Natsheh told Al Jazeera. “Ahead of the Jewish holidays, they sent a message to me and a group of other worshippers, warning us not to approach the mosque or else we will be arrested.”

Even when he is not subject to a formal exclusion order, al-Natsheh said, Israeli police have prevented him from entering Al-Aqsa. He also alleged that officers have repeatedly arrested him at Al-Aqsa’s gates and severely beaten him while in detention.

“The path to the mosque has become incredibly difficult; it is swarming with soldiers and settlers,” he said. “We are denied the ability to reach it with any ease, and if we try, we face arrest and beatings with batons. It is deeply painful to witness what is happening to Al-Aqsa now.”

Al Jazeera has reached out to Israeli authorities for comment, but has yet to receive a response.

Al-Aqsa Mosque has seen an escalation in Israeli restrictions and violations throughout 2026.

After the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran on February 28, Israeli authorities closed Al-Aqsa to most worshippers for 40 days, reopening the compound on April 9.

Meanwhile, according to the Palestinian Authority’s Jerusalem Governorate, almost 28,000 visits by Israeli settlers were recorded at Al-Aqsa between July and September.

Ma’rouf al-Rifai, an adviser to the Jerusalem Governorate, told Al Jazeera that during recent Jewish holidays, Israeli restrictions on Muslim worshippers had intensified.

These measures included closing the mosque for periods of time, preventing noon prayers on at least one occasion, and restricting access for residents of the Old City during visits to the site by Israeli settlers and Jewish religious activists.

Al-Rifai said the Islamic Waqf Department faces mounting constraints on its role in managing the mosque’s affairs.

He said Israeli police have prevented Waqf officials from accompanying Jewish groups when they entered the site, curtailed the authority of mosque guards, and arrested or barred several employees from the compound.

As a result, he said, fewer than 15 guards are now on duty during the morning shift, compared with approximately 50 previously.

He pointed out that the closure of the mosque for 40 days during the war with Iran took place without consulting the Waqf or providing prior notification, which he said demonstrated the Waqf’s diminishing role in the mosque’s administration.

“Settler incursions have undergone a shift over the past three years; they now include Jewish prayers and religious rituals, the raising of Israeli flags, and attempts to bring in sacrificial offerings,” al-Rifai said.

These changes have undermined longstanding arrangements at the compound, under which the Waqf manages Muslim religious affairs while Israeli police oversee security and access.

According to al-Rifai, Israeli authorities have prevented the Waqf from carrying out restoration work at the Bab al-Rahma prayer hall and restricted maintenance of the compound’s trees and gardens. He said the committee responsible for restoration work at Al-Aqsa has been unable to carry out its duties for years.

He warned of efforts to alter the status quo at Al-Aqsa Mosque, pointing to several proposals and developments, including demands to allow Jewish visitors into the compound on Saturdays, plans advanced by Israeli politicians to divide access to parts of the site between Muslims and Jews, and an Israeli police recruitment drive for volunteers tasked with escorting Israeli incursions at the site.

Al-Rifai said these developments represented a further erosion of the Waqf’s authority and warned that they could eventually transform the arrangements governing worship and access at the holy site.

articles.title: CCPA penalises Justdial, Sunrise Foods for safety, misleading product claims
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties on online business directory Justdial and Sunrise Foods for violations
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties on online business directory Justdial and Sunrise Foods for violations involving consumer safety and misleading product claims.While it slapped a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Justdial for allowing listings of ammonium nitrate, a regulated explosive substance, on its platform without adequate safeguards, a Rs 1 lakh penalty was imposed on Sunrise Foods for marketing its bread as “100% Whole Wheat Bread” without disclosing its actual whole-wheat content.In an order on Wednesday, CCPA held that Justdial’s platform carried listings of ammonium nitrate without adequate disclosure of sellers’ valid licences issued by Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), verification of buyers’ eligibility and mechanisms to ensure transaction traceability. The listings also lacked appropriate warnings about legal restrictions on the possession and use of the substance.Justdial argued that it was an online directory and information-listing service, not a trading platform and that the listings were old and sourced from public-domain information or user submissions. However, CCPA held that reliance on vendor representations and removal of listings only after complaints or regulatory intervention was insufficient. It directed the company to immediately discontinue listings, advertising and facilitation of access to the product.In a separate order, CCPA penalised Sunrise Foods for its “Everyday 100% Whole Wheat Bread”. The authority found the product contained only 64% whole wheat, below the prescribed 75% threshold for using the nomenclature “whole-wheat bread”. The packaging did not disclose the proportion of whole wheat, potentially misleading consumers about the product’s composition.Sunrise Foods argued that the “100%” claim referred to the wheat flour component being entirely whole-wheat flour rather than refined flour. However, CCPA said the representation created a misleading impression about the product’s composition. It directed the company to discontinue the claim across print, electronic and social media with immediate effect.It directed the company to immediately discontinue misleading advertisements across media and submit a compliance report within 15 days.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Value of Google parent Alphabet plunges by $500bn as AI fears rattle Wall Street
articles.summary: Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI search summaries were affecting ad revenue.
articles.body:
Google parent Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after it rattled Wall Street with its last update of the year on its business operations.

Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its artificial intelligence (AI) summaries on search were affecting ad revenue.

Microsoft and Amazon also updated investors this week, and joined Google in plans to keep spending astronomical sums of cash in an ongoing AI race.

But investors appeared dismayed at the impacts these plans are having on the ability of each to keep growing their core lines of business.

Google AI is eating its core business - search

At first glance, the quarterly results of Alphabet, the parent company of Google, were not at all bad.

Total revenue grew 25% compared to last year, hitting $127.6bn. It was buoyed by the ongoing success of Google Cloud, where revenue grew by 103% to almost $31bn.

However, profits at the company fell by a considerable 25% during the quarter. And for the second time in its history as a public company, it showed negative free cash flow, this time in excess of $9bn. That's almost twice the loss of cash Alphabet showed just three months ago.

Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Alphabet is now spending more money than it is bringing in. That new level of spending is almost entirely dedicated to Google's AI investments.

By the end of Thursday, the company's total stock market value had fallen to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before.

Google's omnipresent search engine now defaults to AI summaries of a person's query, and that hit the number of advertisements it was able to sell during the quarter.

The sale of ads that appear alongside Google Search results is the vast majority of Alphabet's business.

Tracy Woo, a principal analyst at Forrester, said Alphabet's disappointing search business results "highlights the challenge of funding massive AI investments while maintaining the strength of established businesses."

Although Phillip Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said on Wednesday that he felt "very good about our trajectory" with an AI-focused version of the search engine, the company's stock fell by almost 13% on Thursday, its second lowest showing this year.

Investors not buying Amazon's trillion-dollar business hopes

Amazon's stock also took a hit on Thursday after it shared results that disappointed investors. Shares of the company fell 6% in after hours stock trading.

Alongside quarterly sales growth of 11%, hitting $201bn, the company shared a staggering cash flow figure of negative $42bn.

That number shows that Amazon is not only spending more money than it makes, but that spending has increased six-fold over the span of three months.

Chief executive Andy Jassy claimed the business was spending in part because it had the chance at, not one, but two businesses that could end up bringing in $1 trillion for Amazon the future.

Jassy did not specify what two Amazon businesses those may be. But during a call with financial analysts he repeatedly mentioned the financial opportunity presented by Amazon making and selling its own computer chips, as well as its AI developer platform Bedrock, which offers paying users access to most major AI models and tools.

"One of the lessons we've learned over 20-plus years is that there is not one tool to rule the world," Jassy said. "People always assume whatever is in the lead early on will be the only thing that people use - it's never true."

As Jassy was asked several times to explain the company's spending, he admitted it "would be more convenient" if it were spread over the next 25 years. "That's not the world we live in," he added.

"We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size, the revenue, the free cash flow of Amazon."

Microsoft begs the question of AI's real value

Wall Street reacted less enthusiastically to Microsoft's update, with shares falling by less than 1% on Thursday.

The company, which is also one of OpenAI's largest investors, spent around $5bn less on investments dedicated to AI. It also revealed earlier this week plans to cut thousands of workers , which will further reduce the company's costs.

Meanwhile, its revenue grew 19% from a year earlier, hitting $92.3bn for the quarter. Its crucial cloud business grew by 30% to $63bn.

Chief executive Satya Nadella said the use of Copilot, Microsoft's AI chatbot and tool, has seen "automated tasks nearly double since July" as daily users grew by 500% from a year ago.

Usually lower spending and growing sales earns a positive reaction from investors.

But Woo said Wall Street is trying to look farther into the future when it comes to which businesses will truly make good on their big promises around AI.

"Microsoft's results reinforce that enterprise demand for AI remains strong, but they also highlight a much bigger question facing the technology industry, where AI value will ultimately be captured," Woo said.

articles.title: Spain train crash: Young athlete and former minister among victims
articles.summary: As some of the victims' names are released publicly, an outpouring of grief and anger is sweeping across Spain.
articles.body:
A 24-year-old athlete and a former government minister are among the victims of a deadly train crash that killed 69 people near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday morning.

The crash, between a high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train on the same track, also injured more than 100 people injured, many seriously.

The impact caused carriages to derail, and there are fears the death toll could still rise, with reports of family members searching for missing relatives in hospitals across the region.

The bodies of those killed have been taken to the main forensics institute in Toledo, where families have been giving DNA samples to help identify them.

The crash is the second rail disaster in Spain this year, and the worst in the country's history since 2013.

Julieta Gallego, 24, was a Spanish long jumper who competed for Madrid athletics club, AD Sprint.

"The entire club is heartbroken," it wrote on Instagram.

The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation (RFEF) announced her death , expressing its condolences to her family, friends and teammates.

Gallego regularly competed in Spanish club championships, local media outlet ABC reported , and had a best jump of 5.9m (19ft 3in).

Raúl Chapado, president of RFEF, told the outlet that her death is a "blow that strikes at the very heart of the athletics family."

"Today, the sport mourns the passing of Julieta, a life ahead of her that has been unjustly extinguished".

The death of former employment minister Fátima Báñez, 59, was confirmed by the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE), which she chaired.

"Her warmth, generosity, and commitment leave an indelible mark on businesses and the entire CEOE team," it said in a statement.

Báñez served in the government under former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy from 2011 until 2018, and was the first woman to hold the role. In 2012, she introduced controversial labour reforms that made it easier for companies to fire people, sparking mass protests across the country.

Following news of her death, Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso paid tribute to her, saying she would be "deeply missed".

"Spain loses a great political figure," she said.

The Civil Guard confirmed the death of its officer José Manuel Chacón, 31, in a statement expressing its "deepest condolences" to his family, friends and colleagues.

Finance and tax lawyer, Antonio Montero Domínguez, was remembered as a "meticulous professional" and "tireless worker" by legal news website, El Derecho .

His death was confirmed by Spain's tax authority , where he had been an inspector between 2012-2016.

articles.title: At 99, Pauline Kana became the world’s oldest crowd-surfer; the internet-famous ‘Gangster Granny’ achieved the Guinness World Records title at a Texas concert
articles.summary: At a country-rock concert in Texas, an elderly woman made her way through a sea of raised hands without taking a single step.
articles.body: At a country-rock concert in Texas, an elderly woman made her way through a sea of raised hands without taking a single step. Secured to a stretcher and carried above the audience, Pauline Kana was there to attempt something few people her age would consider. At 99 years and 274 days old, she became the oldest person to crowd-surf, according to Guinness World Records. The June 2026 report described a record attempt organised with help from her grandson, Ross Smith, who has built a substantial online following by sharing videos of their unusual adventures. For Pauline, the concert was another opportunity to take part in the kind of antics that made her an internet favourite.How Pauline Kana became the internet’s Gangster GrannyPauline's online identity, the Gangster Granny, developed through videos made with Ross, whose TikTok account has nearly 25 million followers and whose Instagram account has around 4 million, according to Guinness World Records. Their clips often feature her taking part in playful situations that challenge expectations about what a grandmother might get up to.Some of the videos involve encounters with professional wrestling stars, while others show Pauline appearing at baseball games in a bikini-print T-shirt or displaying cheeky signs in public. Their videos have also introduced Pauline to audiences well beyond her own family. In an interview with Press Pass LA in 2022, she explained that internet attention was unfamiliar territory for someone who had grown up in a period before television and the web became part of everyday life.She described the experience as a positive whirlwind and said the videos had helped people connect with older relatives. Viewers had contacted her to explain that the clips encouraged them to get back in touch with their grandparents, she said.Idea behind Pauline’s unusual Guinness World Records attemptThe record attempt grew out of Ross's interest in finding new experiences for his grandmother. Guinness World Records reported that he wanted Pauline to achieve something she could call a world record, and the pair agreed to try crowd-surfing at a Brantley Gilbert concert in Texas in May 2026.Crowd-surfing usually involves a concertgoer being lifted above an audience and passed along by people supporting their body with their hands. Pauline's attempt used a stretcher, allowing the audience to carry her while she remained secured in place.The setting brought together a live music performance and a planned record attempt. Country-rock musician Brantley Gilbert introduced Pauline and Ross to the audience and explained what they were about to do. Concertgoers then prepared to lift the stretcher and move it towards the stage.Pauline arrived wearing a red-and-white T-shirt printed with her own face and the words “Old's Cool”. The slogan matched the light-hearted approach that had become familiar to her online audience.What happened when the 99-year-old was lifted above the crowdAt the start of the attempt, Pauline held tightly to the sides of the stretcher as the audience raised her overhead. The movement meant she had to rely on the people beneath her to carry her safely through the venue.As the stretcher moved forward, however, she appeared to grow more comfortable with the experience. Guinness World Records described how she began lifting her arms and waving to the audience, smiling as the crowd passed her towards the front.People chanted “Granny! Granny! Granny!” while she travelled above them. The attempt depended on the audience working together to keep the stretcher moving, with numerous concertgoers supporting it along the way.When Pauline reached the front, she emerged from the crowd smiling and joined Ross on stage, where the two danced together. A video shared afterwards showed her holding the Guinness World Records certificate and announcing that she had done it.The achievement was officially recorded as the oldest crowd-surf by an individual, with Pauline aged 99 years and 274 days on the day of the attempt.How the record fits into her life onlineThe record attempt followed years of public attention that Pauline had not experienced during most of her life. Her comments to Press Pass LA in 2022 suggested that she had gradually become accustomed to meeting people through the videos, even as the scale of the audience remained unusual to her.The crowd-surfing stunt took that format into a live setting. Rather than filming another skit for social media, the pair invited a concert audience to participate in an experience that would be documented as a Guinness World Records achievement.Afterwards, Pauline's declaration that she was “the greatest of all time” echoed the playful tone of the videos that had introduced her to millions of viewers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump administration attempts to take down leak of ICE personnel data
articles.summary: An Icelandic web company, FlokiNET, has defended the data’s publication as satisfying a ‘legitimate’ public interest.
articles.body:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has asked an Icelandic web hosting company to take down a site with information about tens of thousands of its employees.

On Thursday, the Icelandic company FlokiNET posted a letter it received from the cybersecurity firm ZeroFox, on behalf of DHS.

The letter accused FlokiNET of violating its terms of service by publishing a “stolen” employee dataset and asked it to “remove or disable” the information.

“The content is live and places more than 40,000 identifiable individuals at risk of harassment, stalking, and physical harm,” the letter said.

FlokiNET said the letter concerned one domain, icepi.cx, which has compiled information about employees from a range of DHS agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

Those agencies have come under intense scrutiny since the start of President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign in 2025.

But the Trump administration has often refused to identify DHS agents involved in specific operations, citing safety risks.

Though FlokiNET said it refused to comply with DHS’s request, it noted that the website’s registrar ultimately suspended the domain. The employee information has since moved to a different domain.

In a statement posted online, FlokiNET defended its decision not to remove the site.

“Federal officers carrying out an enforcement programme are not private individuals while they are carrying it out,” the company said. “The public has a legitimate interest in knowing who is doing that work, under whose authority, and in which office.”

The database was first posted online on Wednesday by Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), a group that showcases leaked government data.

In the past, DDoSecrets has released emails from convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, as well as information from the Israeli Ministry of Justice and police departments in the US.

A hacker group calling itself the “Department of Peace” has claimed responsibility for obtaining and sharing the DHS data.

Since the database was first published, other groups have spread the information elsewhere, including on sites like icepi.cx. As a result, the information is unlikely to be entirely scrubbed from the internet.

The Trump administration, however, has taken an aggressive approach to online platforms purporting to contain information about ICE employees and other agents involved in immigration operations.

Last year, for instance, the US Department of Justice pressured tech giants like Apple to remove apps that track ICE agents, including one called ICEBlock.

The move sparked backlash from Democrats and free-speech advocates, who argued that the public has a right to report on ICE’s movements.

“Blocking access to these apps at the request of the federal government raises the distinct possibility that Apple is working with government to violate its customers’ First Amendment right to record and report on the activities of their government,” Democratic Representative Jamie Raskin wrote in a letter last year, asking Apple to review its decision.

Immigration agents, meanwhile, have taken several steps to conceal their identities during operations, including wearing face masks or street clothes.

That lack of transparency has spurred criticism from human rights groups and immigration advocates, who argue that they have little recourse to pursue allegations of excessive force or impropriety during ICE raids.

Since Trump was sworn in for a second term, at least 25 people have faced gunfire from immigration agents. Six of the shootings have resulted in deaths.

Other cases have involved alleged violations of civil liberties – including unlawful arrests and racial profiling – as well as controversial tactics like car ramming and tackling.

articles.body: The top US military commander in the Middle East held a rare in-person briefing with US president Donald Trump on Thursday to discuss the state of the Iran war, including the effectiveness of Washington’s naval blockade and military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations, according to reports by The Wall Street Journal and Axios.Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command (CENTCOM), met Trump at the White House alongside defence secretary Pete Hegseth, joint chiefs chairman General Dan Caine and other senior officials. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and White House envoy Steve Witkoff also attended, Axios reported, citing two US officials.Cooper briefed Trump on whether the naval blockade was achieving its objectives, the operation to guide oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz towards global energy markets, and the economic pressure campaign being conducted by the military in coordination with the Treasury Department, according to Axios. WSJ separately reported that the meeting covered military options for Iran and came as Washington weighs resuming major combat operations.The rare in-person briefing comes as Trump pursues two tracks: trying to revive negotiations with Tehran while preparing for the possibility of renewed strikes after the US midterm elections. WSJ has reported that US officials have told Arab Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the elections.Trump hinted at the possibility of renewed military action last week. “We may do another little Epic Fury,” he said at a rally, referring to the US-Israeli bombing campaign in the spring. “Or they’ll agree.”Diplomacy continues amid military preparationsRegional mediators led by Qatar are trying to prevent a resumption of hostilities after the midterms and steer Washington and Tehran back towards negotiations. “The mediation is at a very sensitive stage,” a regional source told Axios.Qatari mediators recently delivered a letter from vice-president JD Vance to Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, proposing a restart of negotiations while stressing that any talks would have to address Iran’s nuclear programme, Axios reported. The Journal has also reported that Vance engaged the Iranian hard-liner in an effort to revive peace negotiations.Trump and Vance met on Wednesday to discuss a possible gesture of goodwill towards Iran, such as sending humanitarian supplies, including food and medicine, according to a source cited by Axios. Trump later publicly backed the idea. He has denied directing Vance to initiate peace talks, saying the contact concerned medical supplies.US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said Thursday that Washington and Tehran were “very close” to an agreement to de-escalate tensions. “I think we’re very close to finally getting to a place where we can say, ‘Let’s just have a timeout,’” Barrack told CNN, while cautioning that a comprehensive solution would not come immediately.Iran, however, has continued to demand that Washington lift the blockade, release frozen Iranian funds and allow Tehran to sell oil before nuclear negotiations resume.Pentagon strengthens regional defencesThe Pentagon has laid the groundwork for a possible renewed bombing campaign in recent weeks, deploying additional air defences, munitions and supplies to the Middle East and moving some troops away from bases considered vulnerable to Iranian retaliation.The US Army is also moving an additional Patriot air-defence battery to Israel amid concerns about a shortage of missile interceptors and efforts to replenish supplies.Iran has threatened to strike a broad range of US and Gulf targets in response to any American attack. Tehran has also resumed producing ballistic missiles using stockpiled components in underground facilities and stepped up efforts to target US personnel in the region.The prospect of renewed hostilities has alarmed some US lawmakers. articles.title: House Judiciary report accuses NYC DAs of downgrading charges to protect illegal immigrants from deportation
articles.summary: Letitia James, Melinda Katz and Eric Gonzalez faced pointed questions about a House Judiciary Committee report on immigration-safe plea deals.
articles.body: Three of New York’s top elected officials appeared surprised Thursday when pressed about a House Judiciary Committee report alleging local prosecutors intentionally downgraded charges against noncitizens to protect them from deportation. During a Manhattan press conference, New York Attorney General Letitia James, Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz and Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez faced questions regarding claims that city prosecutors altered or reduced charges to help noncitizens avoid convictions that would trigger removal. "Did any of you order prosecutors to downgrade gun charges to keep illegal immigrants in the U. S., per the Judiciary Committee report?" a reporter asked. MANHUNT UNDERWAY FOR VIOLENT ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO WAS RELEASED UNDER NYC SANCTUARY POLICIES Katz threw her hands up and shrugged in response, the New York Post reported. "Our answer couldn’t help it," Katz said, before a speaker redirected the room, asking for "any other on-topic questions" and moving the news conference along. "We charge any defendant with an illegal firearm with the highest possible charge under the law," a spokesperson for Katz's office told Fox News Digital. The news conference exchange followed the release of a 22-page congressional report detailing widespread practices across New York City prosecutors' offices. According to the document, Katz's office employs an "Immigration Specialist" to help negotiate "immigration-safe" plea deals and reduce past convictions. DOJ OPENS INVESTIGATION INTO SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF SHIELDING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS FROM CONSEQUENCES The report also cited a 2022 memorandum from Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg allegedly instructing prosecutors to seek dispositions that avoid deportation consequences for all misdemeanors and non-carceral felonies. In addition, the report states that the office of Bronx DA Darcel Clark trains prosecutors in "Immigration-Conscious Plea Bargaining." That includes offering non-deportable offenses, avoiding aggravated felony charges and using hypothetical or "legally impossible" charges, such as "attempted reckless assault," which lack legal intent requirements. VIRGINIA SANCTUARY COUNTY IGNORES 1,670 DETAINER REQUESTS OVER 2 YEARS, HOUSE JUDICIARY COMMITTEE FINDS Prosecutors were also allegedly instructed to omit critical details from official conviction records, such as gun involvement, domestic relationships or the age of minor victims, to prevent federal immigration authorities from using them as grounds for removal. After the news conference, a spokesperson for Katz reached out to the Post to deny that leniency is ever shown in weapons cases. "We charge any defendant with an illegal firearm with the highest possible charge under the law," the spokesperson said.
